skill.name: reflect-on-work
skill.description: Guides agents to add concise knowledge updates and reflection notes after completing work.
skill.summary: Captures structured reflections and knowledge updates after AI-assisted work.
skill.author: Clouder0

content.value_statement: Teams lose lessons from completed AI coding tasks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to return concise reflection fields after work.
actual_capabilities: Defines required compact JSON fields for knowledge updates and reflection.
Lists knowledge categories for codebase, convention, decision, and gotcha notes.
Describes confidence levels for captured knowledge.
Provides examples for reflection-only and complete task outputs.
Encourages concise reporting of successful and failed approaches.
limitations: Does not validate generated JSON or enforce schemas at runtime.
Does not store reflections or send them to a database.
Does not analyze files beyond guiding final response structure.
Can add output overhead when a short answer is preferred.

use_cases.title: Close AI Coding Tasks
use_cases.description: Add a consistent reflection block after an agent completes implementation, testing, or debugging work.

use_cases.title: Capture Engineering Knowledge
use_cases.description: Record conventions, decisions, gotchas, and codebase facts that should inform future work.

use_cases.title: Improve Personal Workflow
use_cases.description: Review what worked, what failed, and which repeated patterns should change the next task.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Reflection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use reflect-on-work for this completed task. Summarize one lesson learned and include what worked, what failed, and patterns noticed.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Codebase Learning
prompt_templates.prompt: After this task, use reflect-on-work to capture any codebase, convention, decision, or gotcha learned from the work.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Failed Approach
prompt_templates.prompt: Use reflect-on-work to identify why the first approach failed, what evidence changed the plan, and what pattern should guide future work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Team Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply reflect-on-work to create a concise final reflection for team handoff, including confidence on knowledge updates and repeated workflow patterns.

output_examples.input: A Claude Code session finishes adding tests for an API route.
output_examples.output: The answer closes with a concise reflection about useful test patterns, one failed assumption, and a likely route naming convention.

output_examples.input: A Codex task fixes a bug after trying two different files.
output_examples.output: The response notes the useful search path, the wasted first attempt, and the dependency pattern found during debugging.

output_examples.input: A Claude session completes a refactor for a shared service.
output_examples.output: The final message records the service convention, confidence level, successful strategy, failed assumption, and repeated code organization pattern.

best_practices: Use this skill at the end of real work, not before the task is understood.
Keep reflections brief and specific enough to guide the next task.
Mark uncertain knowledge clearly when evidence is incomplete.
anti_patterns: Do not invent lessons that were not observed during the task.
Do not replace normal task results with only a reflection.
Do not include sensitive project data in knowledge updates.

faq.question: What does this skill add to a final answer?
faq.answer: It adds structured knowledge updates and reflection fields that summarize lessons from completed work.

faq.question: Does it run commands or inspect the system?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains documentation and JSON examples only.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists all three tools as supported.

faq.question: Is this a project memory system?
faq.answer: No. It formats lessons in the response but does not persist them.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after implementation, debugging, research, or review work where lessons should be captured.

faq.question: What should a good reflection include?
faq.answer: It should include what worked, what failed, patterns noticed, and any knowledge learned with confidence.
